```{r,echo=FALSE}
a = sample(2:9,4)*sample(c(-1,1),4,T)

fac1 = paste0("(x+",-a,")",collapse="")
fac1 = gsub("+-","-",fac1,fixed=T)

ach = -9:9

al = paste0("* ",ach,collapse="\n")

sol = rep(0,length(ach))
for(i in 1:length(a)){
    sol = sol+1*(ach==a[i])
}
sol = paste0(sol,collapse="")

```

Question
========

Let function $f$ be a quartic (4th-degree) polynomial shown below as a product of linear factors:

$$f(x)~=~`r fac1`$$

Find all the [roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero_of_a_function) of polynomial $f$. In other words, find all values of $x$ such that $f(x)=0$.

Answerlist
--------

`r al`


Solution
========


See the [zero product property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-product_property).

A polynomial equals zero whenever one of its factors equals zero.

Thus, the roots are `r paste0(a,collapse=" and ")`.
